about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Country Captain (Georgia Curried Chicken with Currants)
recipes.summary: A mild curry-spiced chicken and tomato dish from the American South, with currants and toasted almonds over rice.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes. Lift out. Cook the onion and capsicum for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and currants, return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender. Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until golden.
Serve the chicken over the rice, scattered with the almonds.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Hoppin' John (Southern Black-Eyed Pea and Sausage Rice)
recipes.summary: A Southern one-pot of black-eyed peas, smoked sausage and rice, traditionally eaten for luck.
steps: Brown the sausage in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the onion, capsicum and celery and cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the rice, thyme and cayenne, then the peas and stock. Cover and simmer on low for 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the stock absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Kentucky Hot Brown-Style Open Chicken Sandwich with Cheese Sauce
recipes.summary: Toast topped with chicken, bacon and tomato under a bubbling cheese sauce.
steps: Pan fry the chicken in a little of the butter for 8 minutes, until cooked through. Cook the bacon until crisp and toast the bread.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Stir in 3/4 of the cheese.
Heat the grill. Put the toast in a dish, top with chicken, tomato, bacon and the sauce, then the remaining cheese. Grill for 4 minutes, until browned and bubbling.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten. Classically made with turkey; chicken keeps it simple.

recipes.title: Monte Cristo (Fried Ham and Cheese Sandwich)
recipes.summary: A ham and Swiss-style cheese sandwich dipped in egg and pan fried, served with apricot jam.
steps: Build 4 sandwiches with the ham and cheese.
Whisk the eggs and milk in a shallow dish. Dip each sandwich for a few seconds each side.
Fry in the butter over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Serve with the jam.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Patty Melt (Beef Patty and Caramelised Onion on Rye)
recipes.summary: A griddled beef patty with melted cheese and sweet onion between toasted rye.
steps: Cook the onion in the butter for 15 minutes, until soft and golden.
Shape the mince into 4 thin patties, season and fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until cooked through.
Layer patty, cheese and onion between slices of bread. Toast in the pan for 2 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese melts.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Cheeseburger Pie
recipes.summary: A cheese and onion beef filling baked in a puff pastry case.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the onion and mince for 10 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Stir in the paste and Worcestershire and cool.
Line a 22cm pie dish with 1 pastry sheet and spoon in the mince. Top with the cheese.
Cover with the second sheet, seal the edges and brush with the egg. Bake for 30 minutes, until puffed and golden.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Crumbed Fish Burgers with Yoghurt Tartare
recipes.summary: Crisp panko-crumbed fish in a soft bun with lettuce and a quick tartare, an Australian beach-town favourite.
steps: Mix the yoghurt and pickle for the tartare. Dust the fish in flour, dip in egg and press into the crumbs.
Fry in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes each side, until golden and the fish flakes. Drain.
Toast the buns for 1 minute, until golden, and fill with lettuce, fish and tartare.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Chicken Kyiv (Garlic Butter Crumbed Chicken)
recipes.summary: Crumbed chicken breast filled with garlic and parsley butter that runs out when cut.
steps: Mix the butter, garlic and parsley, shape into a log and freeze for 20 minutes. Cut a deep pocket in each breast.
Stuff with the butter and seal with toothpicks. Dust with flour, dip in egg and coat in crumbs.

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brown the chicken in the oil for 2 minutes each side, then bake for 20 minutes, until cooked through. Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, until tender, and serve alongside.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Pariserbof (Danish Beef Patty with Fried Egg and Capers)
recipes.summary: A seared beef patty on rye with a fried egg, capers, onion and beetroot, a Danish lunch classic.
steps: Mix the mince with 1 tsp salt and pepper and shape into 4 patties. Fry in half the oil for 4 minutes each side, until cooked through.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Set each patty on a slice of rye, top with an egg, capers, onion and beetroot.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Hakkebof (Danish Onion Beef Patties with Gravy)
recipes.summary: Soft beef patties smothered in browned onions and a simple gravy, served with potatoes.
steps: Mix the mince, milk, 2 tbsp flour, 1 tsp salt and pepper and shape into 4 patties. Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender.
Brown the onion in the butter for 12 minutes. Lift out. Fry the patties in the same pan for 5 minutes each side, until cooked through.
Stir the remaining flour into the pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the onion.
Serve the patties with the gravy and potatoes.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Biksemad (Danish Beef and Potato Hash with Fried Egg)
recipes.summary: Crisp fried potato and beef with onion, topped with a fried egg and a splash of Worcestershire.
steps: Boil the potato for 8 minutes, until just tender, and drain well.
Fry the beef in 1 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Lift out. Fry the potato and onion in the remaining oil for 12 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Return the beef with the Worcestershire and heat through for 2 minutes. Fry the eggs separately for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, then top the hash.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Flaeskesteg (Danish Crackling Pork Roast with Potatoes)
recipes.summary: Pork loin with a crackling rind, roasted with bay and served with browned potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan). Dry the rind well and rub in the salt. Set on a rack over a tin with the bay and water.
Roast for 30 minutes, then lower to 180°C (160°C fan) and roast for 1 hour, adding the potatoes for the last 40 minutes.
Rest the pork for 15 minutes. If the rind is not crisp, grill it for 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely.
Carve and serve with the potatoes and pan juices.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Karjalanpaisti (Karelian Beef and Pork Hot Pot)
recipes.summary: A slow-baked Finnish stew of beef and pork with allspice and onion, served with potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Layer the beef, pork, onion and carrot in a casserole with the allspice and bay, seasoning each layer with salt.
Pour in the water, cover tightly and bake for 2 1/2 hours, until the meat is falling apart.
Serve with the boiled potatoes and the cooking juices.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Lihapullat (Finnish Meatballs with Cream Gravy)
recipes.summary: Soft allspice meatballs in a light cream gravy, served with potatoes and lingonberry jam.
steps: Soak the crumbs in the milk for 5 minutes. Mix with the mince, onion, egg, allspice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll into 20 balls and boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender.
Brown the meatballs in the butter for 8 minutes. Lift out.
Stir the flour into the pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes. Add the cream and meatballs and simmer for 6 minutes, until cooked through.
Serve with the potato and jam.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Makaronilaatikko (Finnish Macaroni and Mince Bake)
recipes.summary: A comforting baked macaroni and beef custard, eaten with ketchup in Finland.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Boil the macaroni for 2 minutes short of the pack time and drain. Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, then the mince for 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Mix the macaroni and mince in a greased dish. Whisk the eggs, milk, 1 tsp salt and pepper and pour over. Scatter with the cheese.
Bake for 35 minutes, until the custard is set and golden.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Kroppkakor (Swedish Potato Dumplings with Bacon)
recipes.summary: Soft potato dumplings with a smoky bacon and onion centre, served with melted butter and lingonberry jam.
steps: Cook the bacon and onion for 8 minutes, until crisp and golden. Cool.
Mix the potato, flour, egg and 1 tsp salt into a soft dough. Shape 12 balls, press a hollow into each and fill with 1 tbsp of the bacon.
Close and re-roll. Simmer in salted water for 15 minutes, until they float and are firm.
Serve with melted butter and the jam.
notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Laxpudding (Swedish Salmon and Potato Gratin)
recipes.summary: Layers of potato and onion baked with salmon and dill in a creamy egg custard.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Layer the potato, onion and salmon in a buttered dish, seasoning each layer and scattering with dill.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream and 1 tsp salt and pour over.
Bake for 45 minutes, until the custard is set and the potato is tender.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Pulled Pork Sandwiches with Barbecue Sauce and Slaw
recipes.summary: Slow-cooked pork shredded in smoky barbecue sauce, piled in a soft bun with crunchy cabbage.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Rub the pork with the paprika, cumin and 2 tsp salt. Put in a covered tin with 1/2 cup water.
Roast for 4 hours, until it shreds easily. Shred and mix with the barbecue sauce.
Mix the cabbage, yoghurt and vinegar. Pile the pork and slaw into toasted buns.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Chorizo, Potatoes and Peppers
recipes.summary: A one-tray Iberian bake of white fish over chorizo-flavoured potatoes and capsicum.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potato, capsicum, onion, chorizo, oil and paprika in a tray with the tomatoes and 1/2 cup water.
Roast for 30 minutes, until the potato is nearly tender.
Season the fish, set on top and roast for 12 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains pork. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Pollo Encebollado (Ecuadorian Onion Chicken)
recipes.summary: Chicken braised under a heap of lime-soaked onions until soft and sweet, served with rice.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cumin, garlic and half the lime juice. Brown in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the onion and 1/2 cup water, cover and cook for 25 minutes, until the onion is soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender. Stir the remaining lime into the chicken and serve over the rice.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Machaca con Huevo (Northern Mexican Shredded Beef with Eggs)
recipes.summary: Shredded beef fried with onion, capsicum and tomato, set with eggs and served in warm tortillas.
steps: Simmer the beef in salted water to cover for 1 1/2 hours, until it shreds. Shred finely.
Fry the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the beef and tomato and cook for 5 minutes, until the liquid has gone.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir for 2 minutes, until set. Warm the tortillas and fill.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Pambazos (Mexican Chilli-Dipped Potato and Chorizo Rolls)
recipes.summary: Soft rolls dipped in red chilli sauce and fried, filled with potato and chorizo.
steps: Boil the potato for 10 minutes, until tender. Fry the chorizo for 6 minutes, until cooked through, and mix with the potato.
Warm the passata with the paprika and 1/4 tsp salt for 4 minutes, until thick.
Split the rolls and fill with the chorizo mix and lettuce. Dip the outside in the sauce.
Fry in the oil for 2 minutes each side, until crisp.
notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork and gluten. Dairy-free.
